rows.grounds: compound: duḥsvapna (bad-dream) + śamana (pacifying); neuter singular form functioning as a benefit in the list
compound: kruddha (angry) + svāmi (lord) + citta (mind) + prasādana (propitiating); neuter singular form functioning as a benefit in the list

items.question: What inner disturbances and interpersonal hostilities does this practice pacify?
premises: The practice propitiates the mind of an angry lord.
These effects remove inner fear and external displeasure.
items.inference: Therefore the practice brings mental calm and restores favorable relations.
items.plain_english: It pacifies bad dreams and soothes the mind of an angry master.
